summary: Fever is typically the body's natural physiologic defense response to infection (viral or bacterial).
potential_considerations: Common viral upper respiratory infection (cold or influenza)
Bacterial infections (urinary tract, strep throat, otitis media)
Post-vaccination immune response
Gastrointestinal infection
comfort_measures: Prioritize oral rehydration with water, oral rehydration solutions (ORS), clear broths, or herbal teas
Rest adequately and wear lightweight, breathable clothing
Avoid cold baths or alcohol rubbing (may cause shivering and paradoxically raise core body temperature)
Over-the-counter antipyretics (e.g. Paracetamol) may provide symptom relief if distressing, according to package instructions
monitoring_signs: Fever exceeding 103°F (39.4°C) in adults or lasting longer than 3 consecutive days
Fever in infants under 3 months of age (this is ALWAYS an urgent medical priority requiring immediate emergency care)
New rash, difficulty staying awake, persistent vomiting, or inability to keep fluids down
emergency_triggers: Stiff neck with severe headache and light sensitivity (meningitis warning)

summary: Cough is an essential protective reflex that clears irritants, foreign particles, and secretions from airways.
potential_considerations: Acute viral bronchitis or common cold
Post-nasal drip from allergic rhinitis or sinus congestion
Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) causing micro-aspiration
Asthma or reactive airway disease
Environmental irritants (smoke, dust, pollution, chemical vapors)
comfort_measures: Stay well-hydrated to help thin mucus secretions
Use warm water gargles or honey (1 teaspoon for individuals over 1 year of age; NEVER give honey to infants under 12 months)
Utilize a cool-mist humidifier or steam inhalation
Elevate head slightly during sleep to reduce nighttime post-nasal drip
monitoring_signs: Cough lingering beyond 3 weeks (chronic cough evaluation required)
Yellowish-green thick sputum accompanied by high fever or chills
Unexplained unintentional weight loss or night sweats
emergency_triggers: Coughing up noticeable amounts of blood (hemoptysis)
Severe shortness of breath or audible wheezing / stridor
Inability to speak in full sentences without gasping

summary: Persistent fatigue is a non-specific symptom reflecting lifestyle factors, systemic illness, or physiological strain.
potential_considerations: Sleep deprivation, irregular circadian rhythm, or obstructive sleep apnea (OSA)
Nutritional deficiencies (Iron deficiency anemia, Vitamin B12, or Vitamin D deficiency)
Endocrine issues (hypothyroidism, dysregulated blood sugar / prediabetes)
Post-viral fatigue syndrome or chronic stress / depression / anxiety
Chronic dehydration or deconditioning
comfort_measures: Maintain consistent sleep-wake cycles (7-9 hours of restful sleep)
Ensure steady water consumption throughout the day
Incorporate balanced nutrition with protein, complex carbohydrates, and leafy greens
Engage in gentle daily movement such as walking or stretching
monitoring_signs: Fatigue that does not improve after adequate sleep and lasts over 2 weeks
Unexplained weight changes, cold intolerance, or hair thinning
Pale skin, brittle nails, or lightheadedness when standing
emergency_triggers: Sudden extreme weakness or inability to move a limb
Chest discomfort or breathlessness on minimal exertion

summary: Dehydration happens when your body loses more fluid and electrolytes than you take in.
potential_considerations: Inadequate daily fluid consumption (especially in hot weather)
Fluid loss from prolonged diarrhea, vomiting, or high fever
Excessive sweating during vigorous physical activity
Diuretic medication use or uncontrolled elevated blood sugar
comfort_measures: Sip oral rehydration salts (ORS) or electrolyte solutions slowly in small, frequent amounts
Drink plain water, coconut water, or clear broths
Rest in a cool, shaded environment
Avoid caffeinated energy drinks, alcohol, or excessively sugary beverages which worsen fluid balance
monitoring_signs: Dry, sticky mouth, sunken eyes, or decreased skin turgor
Dark amber or brown urine with very low volume
Persistent dizziness or lightheadedness upon standing up (orthostatic hypotension)
emergency_triggers: Inability to keep any fluids down for over 24 hours
Confusion, delirium, extreme lethargy, or loss of consciousness
Rapid heart rate, rapid breathing, and cold clammy skin (hypovolemic shock warning)

summary: Headaches can range from common tension-type headaches to migraines or secondary causes.
potential_considerations: Tension headache (stress, muscle contraction in neck/shoulders, eye strain)
Migraine headache (pulsating, often one-sided, sensitivity to light/sound)
Sinus pressure or dehydration
Caffeine withdrawal or lack of sleep
comfort_measures: Rest in a quiet, dark, well-ventilated room
Apply a cool or warm compress to forehead or back of neck
Drink a glass of water slowly to address potential dehydration
Gentle neck stretching and reducing screen time
monitoring_signs: Headaches that increase in frequency or intensity over weeks
Headaches that wake you from sleep or worsen with coughing/bending
Headache associated with jaw pain when chewing in adults over 50
emergency_triggers: Sudden, explosive 'thunderclap' headache reaching peak intensity within seconds (worst headache of life)
Headache accompanied by stiff neck, high fever, or confusion
Headache with facial droop, arm weakness, numbness, or difficulty speaking
